title: The Vishnu Purana — the Sanskrit text
author: vyasa
attributionNote: Ascribed to Vyasa and one of the oldest of the Puranas; the critical edition followed here is M. M. Pathak's, published by the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, 1997–1999. GRETIL's e-text is the critically edited text without commentaries.
description: The Vishnu Purana is the Purana of Vishnu and of the world he orders: the six books take the reader from the creation and the divisions of time through the genealogies of the patriarchs, the solar and lunar dynasties and the deeds of the avatars, to the description of the earth, the heavens, the ages and the final dissolution, with the last book devoted to the teaching of yoga and of release through the knowledge of Vishnu. Its account of Krishna's life in the fifth book is the earliest sustained one after the Harivamsha.
historicalContext: Together with the Bhagavata it is the scripture of Vaishnava devotion, and it is the Purana the modern study of the tradition began from: H. H. Wilson's translation (1840) made it the first Purana read in Europe, and its table of contents is the model for the five subjects every Purana claims to treat.
availabilityNote: Complete: the whole Purāṇa in six books, 127 chapters and 6,341 verses, in the critically edited text, streamed from GRETIL at read time. Each passage is one verse, addressed as book.chapter.verse. The transliterated Bombay edition, which carries the Śrīdhara commentary material, is a separate file on GRETIL and is not imported.
